attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: The antecedent 'if this is the end' is kept. The firm part is 'will be sudden and violent'. The months-long allowance is a hedge, and 'next week is crucial' is emphasis, not a deadline.

contract.note: Using the post's own collapse markers is a fair reading. The one-week horizon_interval conflicts with the contract's own statement that this is not a deadline, so it should not be applied as one. 'This is the end' may mean the August 2024 episode specifically.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure of a large March 2026 raise. Continued financing weighs against a qualifying collapse having happened, but it does not establish the antecedent.
Reuters, October 2026: market stress and paused IPOs, while OpenAI keeps fundraising. None of the post's collapse markers is established, and nothing shows how fast or severe an ending was.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast. The packet does not show that the antecedent (an end of the boom under the post's markers) occurred: OpenAI kept raising money, and the October 2026 stress does not amount to a qualifying collapse. With the antecedent unknown and no deadline, the claim is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: An unhedged categorical claim. 'Has peaked' and 'dead-end' commit him to no meaningful further capability gains; 'will not be kept' is a forecast with no deadline. The promises and the cost/sustainability parts are vague.

contract.note: Reading 'peaked' as no meaningful post-publication capability gains is the ordinary sense of the words. The contract scores only that component and leaves the unenumerated promises and the sustainability parts unresolved, which is fair.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, December 2025: verified ARC-AGI-2 scores of 37.6% and 54%, from an independent operator with disclosed methods. That is a substantial gain after publication.
April 2025 baseline from the same benchmark (o3 under 3% on ARC-AGI-2). Together with e1 it shows the gain over 2025.
METR measured about a 55-minute task horizon for Claude 3.7, the highest it had recorded. This corroborates progress, but the confidence intervals overlap.

reviews.rationale: Independent, verified ARC-AGI-2 results rose from under 3% (April 2025) to 37.6% and 54% (December 2025), which contradicts the claim that generative AI 'has peaked'. Under the contract's early-resolution rule this decides the peak component. The vague promises and cost parts stay unresolved and do not save the categorical claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: This is a factual claim about the funding arrangements at the time of the post. 'Welfare recipients' is rhetoric. The checkable core is billions in cloud credits plus reliance on big-tech infrastructure.

contract.note: Requiring amounts that are actually cloud credits, kept separate from cash investment tied to cloud-spend commitments, is defensible but strict. The speaker may have meant 'credits' loosely, and the result turns on this distinction.

evidence.note: OpenAI, 2023: Azure is its exclusive provider and trains its models. This shows dependence but gives no credit amount, and it predates the target period.
Amazon's $4B total investment in Anthropic and its role as primary cloud provider. An investment total is not a cloud-credit amount.
Semafor: some of these investments come as 'cloud credits' or contracts tied to compute spending. Not quantified or split by recipient.
FTC staff report: the partnerships require large cloud spending with the investing partner and give discounted compute. Later and partly redacted; no credit amounts.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows heavy reliance on Microsoft, Amazon and Google infrastructure and investments tied to cloud spending. No source puts a figure on cloud credits received by August 2024, so the 'billions in cloud credits' element, which the contract requires, is not established either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: The antecedent (Google or Microsoft slowing investment) is kept. The claim that venture capital is not the support is explanatory and is not tested separately. There is no horizon.

contract.note: The post's own 'reducing their capex' framing supports reading the trigger as a companywide reduction. A broader reading that counts project pauses could change whether the condition is met.

evidence.note: AP, April 2025: Microsoft is slowing or pausing some early-stage data-center projects. That is project-level, not a companywide cut.
Microsoft, July 2026: CapEx expectations unchanged apart from an accounting change, and FY27 capex expected to grow. The trigger is not met.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not show the antecedent, a companywide reduction in Google's or Microsoft's investment: Microsoft paused some projects but kept its capex plans and expects growth. With the condition not met and no deadline, the conditional forecast cannot be scored.
